issues.failure_explanation: The abstract, introduction and conclusions say unconditional stability is proven and that numerical verification is eliminated. Theorem th:313 holds only under Assumption assu:34 (unique solvability of (10) for all p, h, mu). That assumption is proved only for p=1 and, in Prop. prop:33, for |mu|<pi/T. For p>1 it is justified only by the authors not having seen failures numerically. Likewise Thm. th:42 assumes uniqueness for (30). The paper therefore replaces the earlier numerical check (p<=17) by an unproven, numerically motivated hypothesis; it does not prove stability for all p.

failure_location.quote: We investigate the stability and conservation properties of the method, demonstrating that it preserves both mass and energy at the final time, and it is unconditionally stable.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the stability results as conditional on Assumption assu:34 in the abstract, introduction and conclusions, and drop or qualify the claim of eliminating numerical verification.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claims (unconditional stability for all p, no numerical verification) are stronger than the conditional theorems th:313 and th:42 support.
issues.title: Unconditional stability advertised as proven, but it rests on an unproven (numerically motivated) assumption
issues.why_classification: The claims can be corrected by rewording. The central guarantee is then explicitly conditional, which is a limited weakening and not a collapse of the results.

issues.failure_explanation: By (eq:14), i(psi',w) equals i times a nonnegative real number, so its real part is 0, not the integral of |psi'|^2 e^{-s/T}. The displayed identity is false. As written, the sum also mixes signs when mu<0, so psi=0 does not follow for mu<0. The correct argument takes the real part (mu times a positive quantity vanishes, giving psi=0 for mu≠0) and the imaginary part (for mu=0).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split the identity into real and imaginary parts, or invoke uniqueness for the linear ODE.
issues.overall_effect: The stated proof of uniqueness at the continuous level is invalid as written. The result itself is true, e.g. by ODE uniqueness.
issues.title: Continuous uniqueness proof takes the real part of i*(positive quantity)
issues.why_classification: A short local repair preserves the statement and nothing else depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed expansion shows q^C is anti-palindromic: q^C(1/z)=-z^{-2p}q^C(z). A palindromic plus an anti-palindromic polynomial is not reciprocal, so 'xi root implies 1/xi root' is false for q^K. Also K=iB-rho*C gives q^K=i q^B - rho q^C, not (25). The zeros of q^K are in fact symmetric under xi -> 1/conj(xi), which uses the factor i and real coefficients. That symmetry would give type (l,2p-2l,l), but the argument given does not prove it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'reciprocal' by the reflection symmetry xi -> 1/conj(xi), prove it from q^K=i q^B - rho q^C with real coefficients, and correct (25).
issues.overall_effect: The step from 'two unit-modulus zeros' to weak well-conditioning is unsupported as written. The type claim is probably salvageable.
issues.title: Symbol polynomial of K is not reciprocal; q^C is anti-reciprocal and (25) drops the factor i
issues.why_classification: A short computation gives the corrected symmetry and the same zero-type conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For~$\rho>0$ and~$p \in \mathbb{N}$, the function $K_p(\theta,\rho)$ has exactly 2 simple zeros

issues.failure_explanation: Prop. prop:312 is proved only for rho>0. For rho=0, K_p=-B_p has a double zero at theta=0 (B_p'(0)=0), so the 'two simple zeros' count fails. The case rho<0, needed for negative eigenvalues mu_j of the Hamiltonian, is never treated; it would follow from K_p(-theta,rho)=K_p(theta,-rho), but this is not stated. Step 2 of the outline also asks only for rho>0.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the parity relation to cover rho<0, and treat rho=0 separately (double zero at z=1, with B_n invertible).
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is established only for rho>0, whereas the stated range covers all mu in R, including negative mu.
issues.title: Main stability theorem claims all rho in R, but the zero-count proposition covers only rho>0
issues.why_classification: Short routine arguments fill the missing cases without changing the method or the claim.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem th:313 says that for each fixed rho the family {K_n(rho)}_n has condition number at most a power of n. The constants and exponent from Thms. th:38 and th:39 depend on the symbol, hence on rho. In the actual scheme mu is fixed and rho=mu*h=mu*T/(n-p+1) changes with n. For the fully discrete method, mu ranges over the discrete spectrum, which is unbounded as h_x->0, so rho is unbounded for fixed h_t. Stability for the scheme requires bounds uniform in rho (near 0 and for large rho), and none is given. Fig. 0 tests only rho in [1,100].

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove uniformity of the conditioning bounds in rho, for example by quantifying the distance of the zeros of q^K from the unit circle over rho in R and the behaviour as rho->0 and rho->infinity. Otherwise restate the theorem as a per-rho result.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that (10), and hence (7), is unconditionally stable, i.e. algebraic growth in 1/h uniformly in mu, h_x and p, is not supported.
issues.title: Pointwise-in-rho weak conditioning is equated with unconditional stability, although rho=mu*h varies with n
issues.why_classification: The missing step needs a contained new uniform estimate, or a weakened statement. The overall approach survives.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma a1 bounds kappa(S) by kappa(M) for the Schrodinger-type block matrix. So stability of (32) gives a well-conditioned Schur complement S. The proof then needs the converse, that a well-conditioned S gives a well-conditioned wave matrix [[B,C],[-mu_w C,B]]. The converse is not proved and does not follow from Lemma a1. It requires an upper bound on ||M^{-1}|| via the inversion formula, or a different argument, together with control of the dependence on mu_w. In addition, equating the problems requires mu_w=1 in (30), while the proof uses general mu_w.

failure_location.quote: Hence, the weakly well-conditioning of these Schur complements implies the stability of formulation~\eqref{eq:30} for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the reverse inequality from the block inversion formula, or use the diagonal similarity diag(1,sqrt(mu_w)) relating the two matrices in (33). Then track the mu_w-dependence of the constants.
issues.overall_effect: The alternative proof of unconditional stability of the wave method of the earlier reference is not established as written.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem th:42 infers conditioning of the wave system from its Schur complement, the reverse of Lemma a1
issues.why_classification: A contained extra lemma or argument is needed, and the theorem's claim is expected to survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Factor iB⊗M + C⊗A = (iB⊗I)(I⊗M + G⊗A) with G=(iB)^{-1}C=QRQ^H. Step 4 should then involve I⊗M + R⊗A and a right-hand side carrying a factor -i from (iB)^{-1}. Instead it uses R^{-1}⊗M, and steps 2 and 5 omit the factor i. As stated, step 4 is not equivalent to (35). Moreover (35) has +C⊗A, whereas K=iB-mu*C with A having eigenvalue mu*M (Remark rem:32) gives iB⊗M - C⊗A.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rederive (35) with the correct sign from (19), and rewrite steps 2, 4 and 5 so that the Schur-transformed system is I⊗M + R⊗A with the proper factor i.
issues.overall_effect: Taken literally, the solver computes a solution of a different system than (35), and (35) has the wrong sign relative to the analysed matrix.
issues.title: Algorithm 1 does not solve the linear system (35), which is itself inconsistent with (21)
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local re-derivation of one step and the signs, with no change to the method's guarantees.
